title: fix(auto-reply): message-tool replies from Slack threads post at the channel root on CLI runtimes
body:
Closes #160749

## What Problem This Solves

An agent on a CLI runtime (for example `claude-cli`) posts at the Slack channel root when it calls `message` without `threadId` during a turn that started in a thread.

## User Impact

Untargeted message-tool replies from Slack thread turns stay in the thread on CLI runtimes, as they already do on the embedded runtime. Explicit root sends and different channel targets keep their existing behavior. Standalone turns keep their current routing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI candidate passed the raw inbound reply mode into the CLI run and MCP grant. On Slack channels that defaults to `"off"`. The embedded runtime instead asks the channel threading adapter, which upgrades a thread-originated turn to `replyToMode: "all"` and marks it `sameChannelThreadRequired`.

The CLI candidate now resolves the reply route through that same adapter, using the queued reply-route overlay used by the embedded path. When the adapter requires a same-channel thread, the CLI run takes its thread target and reply mode.

Other turns retain their existing CLI route facts. Adopting the standalone message's adapter anchor would change current-source reply classification, the separate embedded-side issue tracked in #142037.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the three changed files (checked current-main history).

Reported and implemented by @maxpuppet; the contributor commit is unchanged.

## Evidence

Tested the unchanged head `d6d82e7a5c5ab50e12401d3e132dfeb0f9c8a596` against current main `40d9ed0924dafa3ef1bf8cf604679e79aa33a3e4` in a secretless Node 24.21.0 Docker container. Each checkout was built through `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> --version`, then ran its real Gateway with separate state/config paths and loopback ports.

A local HTTP Slack API recorded the final `chat.postMessage` requests. Signed Slack HTTP `app_mention` events entered an existing thread with `replyToMode: "off"`. A fake Claude executable, based on the repository's stdio harness, completed the actual Claude protocol handshake and called the Gateway-generated MCP HTTP endpoint using `tools/call` with `name: "message"`. No internal routing helpers or message-tool implementation were mocked.

All IDs below are synthetic:

| Scenario | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI: `{action: "send", message: "P160749_TOOL_SEND"}` in thread `1790800000.000001` | `channel: C12345678`, **no `thread_ts`** | `channel: C12345678`, **`thread_ts: 1790800000.000001`** |
| CLI: explicit `target: "channel:C87654321"` | `channel: C87654321`, no `thread_ts` | Same; originating thread not inherited |
| CLI: explicit `topLevel: true` | `channel: C12345678`, no `thread_ts` | Same; root opt-out respected |
| Embedded runtime: untargeted message-tool send in the originating thread | `thread_ts: 1790800000.000001` | Same |

The embedded control used a local streaming OpenAI-compatible mock provider and the real `tool_call` catalog dispatcher to invoke `message`. CLI MCP receipts also changed from no thread ID on main to `receipt.parts[0].threadId: "1790800000.000001"` on the PR head.

This is isolated Gateway/CLI/MCP/Slack-API boundary proof, not a claim about a real Slack workspace or client rendering.

## Regression Tests

- Candidate: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-sessions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **16 passed**.
- Negative control: copied that test file into the current-main container without changing production code, then selected `keeps untargeted message-tool sends from a thread turn in that thread` — **fails: expected `all`, received `off`**.
- Cost: candidate invocation 57.06s wall including a cold compiled-worker cache (Vitest 52.88s); the new thread and standalone cases took 174ms and 190ms respectively.

The focused argument-boundary regression is supported by the end-to-end transport evidence above; it is not presented as Slack delivery proof by itself.
